sections.h2: What do the PVA, clerk and sheriff each do in Marshall County?
sections.html:
Two of the three offices share 1101 Main Street in Benton: the Property Valuation Administrator and the County Clerk. The sheriff collects the bill. Together they cover valuation, collection and recording.

  • The PVA appraises property and processes exemptions. The county directory lists weekday hours from 8 am to 4:30 pm and 270-527-4767 as an alternate phone.
  • The County Clerk keeps the county's land records and, as the county describes the job, collects delinquent property taxes. The clerk's number is 270-527-4740.
  • The Sheriff's Office collects the county's taxes, and a lookup and payment link sits on its page of the county website.

The sheriff's department covers roughly 300 square miles with more than 900 miles of roads, plus marine patrols on the lake, and also handles court security and legal process alongside tax work.

Anyone whose house stands inside Benton also gets a city bill. The City of Benton collects its own property tax, from City Hall at 1009 Main Street (270-527-8677), and its website warns residents not to pay county taxes through the city link.

sections.h2: How did Kentucky Lake shape Marshall County real estate?
sections.html:
Marshall County is a lake county, and the lake explains most of its modern history. The Tennessee River and Kentucky Lake form its northeastern border. Of 340 square miles, 39 are water. It is the only Purchase-region county that does not touch another state.

The legislature split the county from the northern half of Calloway County in 1842. For its first century the economy was farming, and the population swung hard: 15,215 in 1920, 12,889 in 1930, 16,602 in 1940 and 13,387 in 1950. In the 1940s the Tennessee Valley Authority impounded Kentucky Lake. Fishing resorts followed, and low-cost power from Kentucky Dam brought chemical and manufacturing plants to Calvert City. The impoundment flooded Birmingham and Gilbertsville, and Gilbertsville was rebuilt west of its first site. The county then grew to 20,381 by 1970, 25,637 by 1980 and 30,125 by 2000.

Benton is the seat and largest city. Calvert City and Hardin are the other cities, and Gilbertsville is a census-designated place. Aurora, Draffenville, Fairdealing and Briensburg are among the unincorporated communities. A state marker near Benton commemorates a March 23, 1864 clash between Confederate and Union cavalry. The county sits in the Central time zone, and part of Clarks River National Wildlife Refuge lies inside it. If you own a lakeside or second-home parcel, ask the PVA how it is classified and when it was last inspected.

sections.h2: Who lives in Marshall County, according to the Census?
sections.html:
The county is older and steadier than most of Kentucky. A quarter of residents are 65 or over, and more than four in five homes are lived in by their owners.

Poverty is 10.7 percent, 91.4 percent of adults 25 and older finished high school, and 21.2 percent hold a bachelor's degree. The mean commute is 23.7 minutes. Employer establishments numbered 734 in 2023, employing 9,645 people on a $600.5 million payroll, with employment up 6.3 percent from a year earlier. Retail sales were $638.4 million in 2022, health care and social assistance took in $77.9 million, and transportation and warehousing took in $62.8 million. Another 2,366 businesses had no employees. Foreign-born residents make up 0.9 percent of the population, 7.5 percent of residents under 65 lack health insurance, and 85.5 percent of households have broadband.

sections.h2: Why were Marshall County's 2026 tax bills mailed late?
sections.html:
Rates had to be finalized before the bills could be printed, so the Sheriff's Office announced a collection start of November 1, as Marshall County Daily reported on October 9, 2026. The schedule it published:

  • November 1 to 30, 2026: two percent discount.
  • December 1 to 31, 2026: face amount due.
  • January 1 to 31, 2027: five percent penalty.
  • February 1 to April 15, 2027: ten percent penalty.

The shifted calendar matches the alternative schedule in KRS 134.015(3), which lets the Department of Revenue replace the usual dates when billing runs behind. In an ordinary year the discount ends November 1 and the face amount runs through December.

Whatever the year, the dates on the bill in your hand control. At the end of the cycle unpaid bills move to the County Clerk and begin to carry interest of one percent a month, according to the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: Where does a Marshall County owner turn when a value looks too high?
sections.html:
Go to the PVA's counter and ask for a conference. That is the first step in KRS 133.120. If you leave unconvinced, put your reasons and your own estimate of fair cash value in a petition to the County Clerk within one workday after inspection ends, and prepare for the board hearing described in KRS 133.030.

  1. Collect nearby sales, an appraisal or building costs.
  2. Appear in person or send an authorized representative.
  3. Pay tax on the value you claim while the case is pending.

Skipping the county board forfeits the later state appeal, so the petition deadline matters. Owners with working farmland should ask whether it is valued on agricultural use, as Section 172A of the state constitution allows.

sections.h2: Does Marshall County's older population qualify for the homestead exemption?
sections.html: Many owners do. With 25.1 percent of residents at least 65, the exemption reaches a large share of homes. It is worth $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, which turns the median value of $173,800 into a taxable $124,700. The Marshall County PVA takes the application, with proof of age or a total-disability classification. A buyer who qualifies applies anew, since the benefit follows the owner.

sections.h2: How do the lien and the deed get handled in a Marshall County sale?
sections.html:
A lien from delinquent tax can last up to eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), so unpaid years must be cleared at closing. The County Clerk collects delinquent property taxes in Marshall County, so ask the clerk (270-527-4740) for prior-year payoffs and the sheriff for the current bill.

Deeds are recorded with the same clerk, who first collects the grantor's transfer tax of fifty cents per $500 of value under KRS 142.050. That is $174 on a sale at the county median. The clerk's homepage promotes a program to protect owners against deed theft, which is worth asking about after you sell.

faqs.q: Where can I look up my Marshall County tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the bill lookup and payment link on the Sheriff's page of the county website. For value or exemption questions, ask the PVA at 1101 Main Street in Benton.

faqs.q: Do Benton residents pay a separate city property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Benton collects it separately, at City Hall, 1009 Main Street (270-527-8677). The city's page says not to use its link for Marshall County taxes.

faqs.q: What was the Marshall County discount for 2026 bills?
faqs.a: Two percent on payments from November 1 through November 30, 2026, under the schedule the Sheriff's Office announced. Face amount applied through December 2026.

faqs.q: Which Marshall County office collects delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: The County Clerk, at 1101 Main Street in Benton. The Department of Revenue says interest of one percent a month starts once bills reach the clerk.

faqs.q: What is the Marshall County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: $49,100 off assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, for owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who apply at the PVA.
